title: An over-long line is shortened from the end in the report, title kept
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin (all permissions) at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919) on the What/Why QA build.
  • Require Tech Story (Settings, Work Orders tab) is off.
  • Customer {Customer-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-WW-C154717 Fleet) has a contact person and an asset, {Asset-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-WW-C154717 Truck).
  • Work order {Work-order-1} (for example S2-15440) is open for {Customer-A} and {Asset-A} at {Location-A}, not invoiced.
  • {Work-order-1} has a labor line {Line-1} whose Title is exactly 16 characters (for example ZZAUTOTEST-WW-17) and whose Description is exactly 5,000 characters: the digits 0123456789 repeated 500 times, with no tech story.
  • {Work-order-1} has been completed and invoiced as invoice {Invoice-A} (for example 10234), dated {Invoice-date-A} (for example 13 Oct 2026).
custom_steps:
1. Open the Reports page and click Export Reports (if it is not there, open it from Administration).
  2. Choose the Customer Invoice report.
  3. Set the date range to cover {Invoice-date-A}.
  4. Download the report.
  5. Open the downloaded file in a spreadsheet (for example Google Sheets: File, Import, Upload).
  6. Find the row for {Line-1} on invoice {Invoice-A} and read its ItemDescription cell.
  7. Click an empty cell, type =LEN( then click that ItemDescription cell, type ) and press Enter.
  8. Click another empty cell, type =RIGHT( then click the ItemDescription cell, type ,10) and press Enter.
  9. Read the first 30 characters of the ItemDescription cell.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 6: the cell holds the title, " - ", then the start of the description; it is shorter than the full 5,019 characters (16 + 3 + 5,000).
  • Step 7: the number is 4000 (16 characters of title + 3 for " - " + the first 3,981 characters of the description = 4,000). Plain digits and letters take one unit each, so 4,000 characters is the 4,000 limit.
  • Step 8: the last ten characters are "1234567890": the end of the description was cut, and nothing trails after it (no hyphen, no space).
  • Step 9: the cell starts with the full title and " - 0123456789" (with the example title "ZZAUTOTEST-WW-17 - 0123456789"): the title survives whole.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-11257; story SV-10132 (Story 3, What Reaches QuickBooks); PRD "What Are You Doing / Why Are You Doing It (What/Why)", Confluence 845348896, version of 13 Oct 2026, S3-R7, S3-R8, read 13 Oct 2026; design canvas board 2.2 (The long end), 13 Oct copy; tech plan "Title and Description - Technical Implementation Plan" (dated 2026-09-23, shared by the QA lead 13 Oct 2026), FR-011; Product comment by Chris Ward, 23 Sep 2026 (Confluence comment 883261444); Source-verified 13 October 2026; not yet build-verified (a What/Why QA build exists; verification by the build verification session).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S3-R7: “When the joined text is longer than 4,000 bytes it is shortened from the end to fit, and it is never cut in the middle of a character. The live sync and the downloadable report are both cut at that same limit, so S3-R4 holds on a long line too. Today only the live sync cuts, and it cuts by bytes without regard for where a character ends; the report has no cut at all. Because the title leads and the narrative trails, the title always survives and the narrative is what gets clipped first.”
  • S3-R8: “The values themselves are unchanged. Nothing is trimmed, truncated, re-cased or escaped that is not trimmed, truncated, re-cased or escaped today, other than the shortening described in S3-R7.”
  • Tech plan FR-011: “If the joined text exceeds 4,000 bytes it is shortened from the end, never mid-character, on both routes; title survives; an over-long line still syncs (S3-R7, S3-R7a, S3-E3).”
  • SV-10132 acceptance criteria: “Given a joined text longer than the QuickBooks limit, when it is sent, then it is shortened from the end, the cut does not fall inside a character, the title is intact, and the invoice syncs rather than landing in Unexported Items.”
